flags.note: C echoes 'pieces missing' from P1, a mild word-echo cue; distractors are all clearly off-scope, so item is easy.

R050-01.notes: Arc: P1 misconception -> P2-3 lesson -> final line 'what the viewer should keep'. A is the rejected early view; B too narrow (dialect only one detail); D unsupported ('long career', 'today'). No defensible alternative.

R050-02.notes: P2: 'filled four lines, stayed on screen for less than five seconds... unreadable.' B reverses (narrator translated every insult); C confuses the source dialect with the subtitle; D conflates later joke-replacement anecdote. No alternative holds.

flags.note: 'force of the speech' slightly extends beyond 'that she won', but no competing option is defensible.

R050-03.notes: A is exactly what the supervisor rejected; B unsupported; C reverses (she won). D captures outcome over content.

flags.note: C is a plausible overstatement lure (gestures 'say things that no subtitle could'), but the passage never claims gestures matter more than dialogue in general; adequately distinct.

R050-04.notes: P3: 'Every word I add pulls the viewer's eyes away from the actors' faces, where much of the meaning lives.' A: training not described; D: comedy introduced in P2.

flags.note: B 'survives' is the common-meaning lure for 'lives'; not defensible in context ('where much of the meaning lives' = resides/is located).

R050-05.notes: Meaning resides in the faces = is found there. C/D don't fit.

flags.note: C echoes 'at the same moment the original audience had' closely (word echo cue). D is a specific-detail lure that mistakes the example for the criterion.

R050-06.notes: Criterion is joke 'does the same work in the scene'; success shown by laugh at the same moment. A contradicts; B irrelevant to jokes; D over-literal.

R050-07.notes: 'a subtitle reading "Good morning" may be enough, because the warmth is in the actor's voice.' C is the opposite case (the pun) in the same paragraph — good contrast lure, not defensible. B, D unsupported.

R050-08.notes: P5: film audience 'hears the actors' real voices beneath every line... anyone watching knows that I have made a choice.' B twists 'test audience' detail; A contradicts; C unsupported.

flags.note: Wording: 'accepting of them' — pronoun 'them' has no plural antecedent in the stem ('what is lost'); reads awkwardly. Suggest 'accepting of the losses while redefining...'.

R050-09.notes: 'I still lose things, of course. But I no longer think of my job as deciding what to throw away.' A too negative (narrator calls subtitles more honest, not lesser); C contradicted by 'I still lose things'; D unsupported.

R050-10.notes: Final sentence reframes job as 'deciding what the viewer should keep.' A reverses; B no new problem; D unsupported. Correct answer is a natural paraphrase.
